title: Airstream Classifier
description: The learner sorts ten airstream cards into clean air or one of four contamination threats (solids, corrosives or moisture, flammables, fumes hazardous to people); the first placement is scored, a missed card stays up for unscored retries, and a summary lists every first choice beside the correct bin.
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: Airstream

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Classifying airstreams as clean or contaminated, and by threat
learningObjectives: The learner will distinguish clean airstreams from contaminated ones and assign each contaminated airstream to its main threat category, with at least 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: In the airstream versus out of the airstream

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); each card, verdict and the summary announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs with solid/dashed borders pair with colour; the revealed bin is marked with → on its button and an outline; bin buttons have aria-labels with the bin name; keys A-E or 1-5 place, Enter goes to the next card; focus moves to Next card after a correct placement.

controls.label: A Clean / B Solids / C Corrosive / D Flammable / E Fumes
controls.purpose: Place the card in that bin (keys A-E or 1-5)

controls.label: Next card / Show summary
controls.purpose: Go on once the card is in the correct bin (Enter)

controls.label: Start over / Sort again
controls.purpose: New round of all ten cards in a new order, score cleared

rules: Each card has exactly one correct bin
Shuffled order, seeded once per session (page load); Sort again continues the seeded sequence
The first placement is scored; a missed card takes unlimited unscored retries until it is placed correctly
The correct bin is revealed after the second wrong placement
Mastery: 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt
assumptions: Each airstream is classified by its main threat
limitations: Real airstreams can carry more than one threat; the cards are chosen to have one main threat each

sources: Card 2: FanPedia p. 32 (radial bladed paper handling impeller)
Card 7: Chapter 1 section 'Air Temperature' and FanPedia pp. 110-116 (high-temperature construction)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Item-by-item classification with an immediate reason, retry to correct, and a first-choice summary
keyQuestions: What is in this air, and why does it matter to the fan?
Is high temperature alone a contaminant?
Can an airstream be a concern even when it does not harm the fan?
commonMisconceptions: Hot air is contaminated air; in fact hot clean air is clean, with its own temperature concerns.
Any airstream from a factory is contaminated.
If the fan survives the airstream, the airstream is not a concern; hazardous fumes are a concern for people even when they do not harm the fan.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt correct: n of 10'; mastery is 8 of 10 on the first attempt.
Retries after a miss are practice, not evidence
